outcome: As of 11 Oct 2026 the grand Riemann hypothesis is not settled: there is no accepted proof and no accepted counterexample. Since 26 Jan 2024 the record holds partial results on zeros of automorphic L-functions that do not say where all of their nontrivial zeros lie: unconditional proportion-on-the-line bounds for ζ, for primitive Dirichlet L-functions and for a degree-3 twisted family (Alpöge and Furman, Aug 2026; Johns, Sep 2026; Hua and Yang, Aug 2026; Conrey, Kwan, Lin and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Jul 2026); zero-free regions and real-zero exclusion for Dirichlet, Hecke and Rankin–Selberg families (OpenAI, 6 Oct 2026, unrefereed; Thorner and Zhao, Jan 2026); conditional results (Dong, Wattanawanichkul and Zaharescu, twice; Basak, Thorner and Zaharescu); one finite computation (Lu, Zaman and Zhao); and unrefereed claimed proofs of the grand RH (Zhang, Preprints.org, not read because the host refused access) and claimed proofs or disproofs of the Riemann hypothesis for ζ alone, none accepted.
problem_asks: Statement (Wikipedia Jan 2024): do the nontrivial zeros of all automorphic L-functions lie on the critical line 1/2 + it with real t? Part by part: (a) the family: every automorphic L-function in Langlands' sense (L-functions of cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over number fields); the statement names no degree, field or twist restriction, so the special cases are included: the Riemann zeta function ζ (trivial character, so this case is the RH itself), all Dirichlet L-functions (GL(1) over Q, all characters including imprimitive and real ones), Hecke L-functions over number fields, and GL(2), GL(3) and higher. (b) the objects: the nontrivial zeros of each such L-function, meaning zeros in the critical strip, not the trivial zeros. (c) the claim: each such zero has real part exactly 1/2. (d) the answer is yes if (c) holds for every automorphic L-function, and no if one nontrivial zero off the line exists for some automorphic L-function. Not asked by this bullet: multiplicity or simplicity of zeros, proportions of zeros on the line, zero-free regions short of the line, bounded height, function-field analogues, or the 'modified' grand RH that allows zeros on the real line, which Wikipedia mentions as a variant but which is not the bullet's statement. Note for the judging pass: a real Siegel zero β in (1/2, 1) of a Dirichlet L-function would be a counterexample to the bullet as worded, though the 'modified' variant would allow it.

disputes.summary: The 67.25% zeta bound (simple zeros on the line) is credited in different ways: Anthropic and its arXiv comments credit Claude with the argument and Alpöge and Furman with verification; Lamzouri's abstract credits 'an internal research version of Claude' with the bound and Alpöge and Furman with verification; Knausgård's introduction credits Claude with the earlier 0.83625 bound. Not a conflict over the same statement, but the arXiv listing names Alpöge and Furman as authors while the title footnote and comments say the argument was discovered by Claude.

The OpenAI 7/8 and 11/12 claims: secondary sources disagree on which manuscript states 7/8 and which 11/12. The repository's CONTENTS entry for the 11/12 alternate proof and the README's human-editing sentence are the only primary text read; the abstracts were not read.
Johns's reviewers: the Zenodo record I fetched names no reviewer; the GitHub VERIFICATION page names an external reviewer 'Astra'. The two pages were fetched in this run and disagree on this point.

Zhang's grand-RH scope changed between versions per search snippets: v5 'modular form L-function, automorphic L-function, etc.' and v6 'all L-functions'. The Preprints.org text could not be read to confirm this.

Zhang's first posting date is uncertain: the identifier 202506 suggests a June 2025 upload, a search snippet reports an earlier version posted 21 Jul 2025, and another snippet dates a companion to September 2025.
Hua and Yang's companion arXiv:2609.27808 carries a 2609 identifier but a listing date of 18 Aug 2026. Unresolved.
Alpöge–Furman: the blog's 41.6→67.2% figure concerns zeros on the line, while the arXiv headline concerns zeros that are simple and on the line (2/3). Secondary coverage often merges them.

AxiomMath's formal certificate for Lamzouri's proof assumes the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula and the BGST pair-correlation formula, while the Lamzouri abstract calls the proof unconditional. Both are recorded; not reconciled.
Knausgård's title gives 67.35% for simple zeros on the line, while the abstract says 'Hence more than 67.80% are simple' (the simple-anywhere-in-the-strip figure). Not reconciled.

summary: Nothing in the window settles the bullet as worded, and the record is not complete for the reasons given under incomplete. The bullet asks one universal yes/no question: does every nontrivial zero of every automorphic L-function have real part 1/2? Every in-window result I opened is partial. The proportion-on-the-line results are unconditional for ζ and each fixed primitive Dirichlet character (Alpöge and Furman, 13 Aug 2026, arXiv:2608.13637; Lamzouri's second proof of the ζ bound, 2 Sep 2026; Knausgård's ζ bounds, 6 Oct 2026), averaged over Dirichlet families (Johns, Zenodo, 30 Sep 2026, weighted at least 0.9322 − ε; Hua and Yang, 17 and 18 Aug 2026, prime modulus, constants 0.6725 and 0.8362), or over degree-3 twists (Conrey, Kwan, Lin and Turnage-Butterbaugh, 1 Jul 2026, at least 1/9 for twists by primitive Dirichlet characters, unconditional for self-dual forms). The region and exclusion results cover ζ, Dirichlet and Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3), and Rankin–Selberg families: the OpenAI family 003 manuscripts (6 Oct 2026, public; manuscripts dated 30 Sep to 5 Oct) give zero-free regions Re s > 7/8 and Re s > 11/12 and a uniform real-zero exclusion, all unrefereed; Thorner and Zhao (7 Jan 2026) give region-type exclusion of real zeros for new Rankin–Selberg families. Two conditional results (Dong, Wattanawanichkul and Zaharescu, Dec 2025 and May 2026; Basak, Thorner and Zaharescu, 2024) do not count as progress without their hypotheses, and Lu, Zaman and Zhao (3 Feb 2026) is a finite check of quadratic characters to modulus 10^10, which by the dataset's rule moves nothing. Read strictly, none of these in-window results gives the statement for any automorphic L-function beyond ζ and primitive Dirichlet characters, and for Dirichlet L-functions even the full case is not settled: the Dirichlet results are partial, and the non-Dirichlet automorphic L-functions are untouched. The only in-window claims of the grand RH itself are unrefereed: Zhang's Preprints.org manuscript(s), which I could not read because Preprints.org, ResearchGate and Sciety refused access, so I rely on search snippets that report an exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros and a scope change from automorphic to all L-functions between versions; I found no expert reading. The RH-only and ζ-only claims are many and mostly unrefereed or withdrawn: Kubalalika (ζ off-line claim, revised Feb 2026), Liu (April 2024), Zhou (SSRN, mirror only), Abe (2022, revised 2026), Davlatov (withdrawn May 2026), and Blinovsky (GRH dropped from v13 in Dec 2025). Each would bear on the bullet directly if it were a counterexample, because ζ is an automorphic L-function, so a disproof of RH would falsify the bullet's 'yes' answer, while a proof of RH settles only the ζ case. Agélas's 2019 GRH claim was refuted in its key lemma by Brent in 2021 (read from the abstract). On AI: the authors of the in-window ζ and Dirichlet proportion papers credit Claude, Anthropic's model, with the mathematics. Alpöge and Furman's arXiv comments say 'Proof discovered autonomously by Claude (Anthropic)', and §1.5 says 'The author of this paper is a large language model developed by Anthropic'; Johns's Zenodo record says the mathematics was 'produced by AI agents (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5) under the author's direction'; OpenAI's README says 'the vast majority of results' came from 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model', with the 11/12 writeup named as human edited for readability; Knausgård's abstract says 'AI-assisted' without naming a system. Lamzouri's own proof is human, with AxiomProver credited for a formal certificate (secondary sources, not read in the PDF), which by §5.4 I recorded but did not list as a system. The Conrey et al., Hua and Yang, Thorner and Zhao, Dong et al., Basak et al., and Lu et al. abstracts carry no AI statement. Close calls: (1) for Alpöge and Furman I dated the event to the arXiv v1 (13 Aug 2026), not the blog (10 Aug), because the blog is an outline; (2) for OpenAI I dated public release (6 Oct 2026), while the manuscripts are dated 30 Sep to 5 Oct; (3) whether Johns and the Hua–Yang papers 'move a quantity the bullet names': the bullet asks a yes/no about all zeros, and a weighted proportion moves the fraction on the line, not the universal claim, so I recorded the direction and left the call; (4) Dong et al. 2512 is conditional on unspecified conditions and I recorded it; (5) Lu et al. is an instance count of a universal claim and I recorded it as discounted. Both readings of each are in the events.
competing_reading: Read generously, the window already contains real movement on the bullet's quantity: the number of zeros off the line of automorphic L-functions has been bounded away from total for ζ, for each fixed primitive Dirichlet character, for a weighted Dirichlet family, and for degree-3 twists, and OpenAI's region results give zero-freeness for Hecke L-functions over Q(√−3). A judge could count the Dirichlet and PGL(3) proportion results as partial resolutions of a restricted case, and the AI involvement in these is load-bearing by the authors' own words. Read strictly, none of this changes the question 'do all zeros of all automorphic L-functions lie on the line?': the proportion results are silent on the zeros they leave off the line, the zero-free regions say nothing about the line, and the only candidate for the full claim is an unreviewed manuscript (Zhang) that no expert has been reported to check.
what_would_settle_it: For the bullet as worded: a refereed proof covering all automorphic L-functions (the Zhang manuscript, or any successor, accepted by specialists), or a verified zero off the line of some automorphic L-function. A ζ-only counterexample (Kubalalika, Liu, Zhou if they survived checking) would settle the bullet in the 'no' direction, since ζ is automorphic. For the partial items: peer review of Alpöge–Furman (and whether the journal version repeats the Dirichlet extension), of Johns and of Hua and Yang; a Lean check of the Dirichlet extension in Alpöge–Furman (the abstract says it is formally verified, the repository does not show it); the AxiomProver appendix of Lamzouri's paper; the OpenAI 7/8 and 11/12 manuscripts' text and abstracts, and an expert check of the Lean statements against the papers; the full text of Zhang's manuscripts (Preprints.org was not accessible), its version history (the v5 to v6 scope change), and any referee report.

judgement.why: The statement is one universal claim over all automorphic L-functions. Proportion-on-the-line results (Wu, Sono, Alpöge–Furman, Lamzouri, Knausgård, Hua–Yang, Johns, Conrey et al.) and zero-free regions (Thorner–Zhao, OpenAI family 003) move quantities without deciding any L-function's zeros, so they are bound. Conditional results (Basak et al., Dong et al. twice) are none, Lu–Zaman–Zhao is instances, Brent is a critique (none), and Math Inc's function-field RH is a variant. Claimed RH proofs for ζ are case and claimed RH disproofs are whole-refuting, but all of them carry several F10 signals or were withdrawn or refuted. Zhang's grand-RH claim is not_credible: scope grew between versions, there are many versions, and nobody has taken it up. AI: Alpöge–Furman and Johns are generated on explicit quotes. The OpenAI items are generated on the repository's general attribution. Lamzouri and Knausgård credit no system in their own events.
judgement.doubts: The OpenAI attribution is a close call. The README says the zero-free-region work for zeta was an exception to the fixed procedure, so the human role in the 7/8 paper is unclear. I answered generated because the repository credits the model and names no human mathematician. openai-math-003 duplicates the 7/8 and 11/12 events. For Alpöge–Furman, Conrey and Goldston examined the paper only per Anthropic's own report, which I did not treat as digestion. Zhang's text was never read. Math Inc and Zhang's RH preprint are undated.
